headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP and shared file surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risks when paired with Chatwoot’s customer-support data flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can use MCP and browsers, and Chatwoot ingests support content and integrations; if Chatwoot outputs are copied into TREK or routed through a shared MCP/file channel, prompt injection becomes plausible. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are forwarded into TREK via MCP, browser automation, or shared files
IF TREK treats imported support text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic import of Chatwoot transcripts into TREK
Require a human review step before TREK acts on copied support text
Strip instructions and markup from transferred text
Use separate workspaces for support and travel-planning tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets. TREK also has file surfaces and browser/MCP egress, so a shared workspace or copied content can expose sensitive data beyond the originating agent.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are placed in a workspace TREK can read
IF TREK uploads or transmits copied files, logs, or secrets from its workspace
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot and TREK on separate hosts or containers
Remove sensitive files from TREK uploads and logs
Restrict TREK network egress to required destinations only
Rotate any secrets that may have been copied into shared storage
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and API integrations, while TREK has allowlisted egress, browsers, MCP, and real-time collaborative multi-instance sessions. Overlapping mutable surfaces create coordination risk even without explicit filesystem write claims; uncertainty about write scope means the safer medium choice is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external service or shared account
IF TREK instances and Chatwoot integrations operate on the same mutable records without locking
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable accounts or databases
Stagger writes so only one agent updates a resource at a time
Review integration scopes before enabling them
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream content; Chatwoot produces customer-support messages and reports that could be treated as authoritative if forwarded. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so a mistaken Chatwoot output can cascade into TREK decisions.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is used as input to TREK planning or automation
IF TREK executes actions without a separate verification step
mitigations: Require TREK to cite source provenance before acting
Add a human approval gate for any downstream action
Do not forward raw Chatwoot summaries into automated workflows
Use checklists to verify dates, reservations, and contact details
requires-engineering: implement validation against source records

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while TREK handles email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, MFA secrets, and logs. The profiles do not document residency or retention alignment, so mixed handling of regulated or sensitive data creates a compliance mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF customer-support records and travel records are stored together
IF TREK logs or uploads retain personal data longer than Chatwoot policy allows
mitigations: Separate retention policies by data class
Purge logs containing personal data
Keep regulated customer records out of TREK uploads
Document data residency for both systems
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across both agents
